plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of blush-white, almond-scented blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Each petal falls in a soft drift, so the ground looks as pretty as the trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-March to mid-April in warmer parts of its range, with peak bloom in many cities in late March. Some southern Japanese cities, including Fukuoka, may see the first blooms around mid-to-late March.
plants.location: Southern Japan, including Kyushu, and warm-climate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.funFact: Cherry blossom forecasting is a national pastime in Japan. Every spring, the 'cherry blossom front' moves north across the islands, and millions of people gather for hanami, the tradition of picnicking under the blooms.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A trumpet of golden yellow sits inside a ring of paler petals. Wild daffodils bloom in woodland and meadow clearings, and in a good year they carpet the ground in gold.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to April in Western Europe, with many populations in full flower in mid-March
plants.location: Woodlands and meadows of England, Wales and Western Europe
plants.funFact: Daffodil bulbs contain a compound called galantamine, which has been developed into a medicine for the symptoms of Alzheimer's disease. The same bulbs are toxic if eaten, which is one reason deer and rabbits leave them alone.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: The largest flower head in the protea family looks like a bowl of silky pink petal-like bracts around a crown of fine, pale center hairs. It grows on rocky mountain slopes in the fynbos, where it stands out against the scrubby green.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late summer to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak flowering from about February to June in some areas. March can be a time when flowers appear in some regions, but timing varies by location.
plants.location: Fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower. Its thick, fire-resistant stems let it survive the wildfires that regularly sweep through the fynbos, and it regrows from underground woody tissue.
